!NotRocketScience is an open-source, web-based aerospace CAD workstation and numerical flight simulator designed to democratize rocketry education and flight safety. Built with React 18, Three.js, and WebGL, the platform eliminates complex desktop software installations, allowing students, amateur rocketeers, and engineers to design, analyze, and simulate rockets directly within any modern web browser.

The platform pairs a cinematic orbital descent powered by authentic NASA 8K Blue Marble, Black Marble, and MODIS atmospheric imagery with an interactive aerospace engineering suite. ### 1. What does it do or how does it work?

**!NotRocketScience** is an open-source, web-based aerospace engineering CAD workstation and flight simulator designed to make rocket science accessible, interactive, and mathematically rigorous.

The platform works through two integrated environments:

1. **The Cinematic Orbital Launchpad**: An interactive 3D WebGL experience built with Three.js and React Three Fiber. Users experience a scroll-driven orbital descent from deep space into low-Earth orbit, featuring authentic NASA 8K planetary textures, dynamic atmospheric cloud layers, and real-time telemetry HUDs.

2. **The Aerospace CAD & Flight Simulation Engine**:

- **Parametric 3D CAD Modeling**: Users design rockets component-by-component (tangent ogives, von Kármán minimum-wave-drag nose cones, transitions, body tubes, trapezoidal fins with airfoils, and recovery systems) with real-time 3D blueprint visualization, cross-section cutaways, and longitudinal slicing.

- **Barrowman Aerodynamics Core**: Instantaneously computes the vehicle’s Center of Pressure ($X_{cp}$) and normal force coefficient derivatives ($C_{N\alpha}$) using the Barrowman method, alongside dynamic Center of Gravity ($X_{cg}$) tracking to calculate the **Static Stability Margin** in calibers ($S = \frac{X_{cp} - X_{cg}}{d_{\text{ref}}}$).

- **RK4 Numerical Integrator**: Simulates 3-DOF and 6-DOF atmospheric trajectories using 4th-Order Runge-Kutta (RK4) integration with an International Standard Atmosphere (ISA) barometric lapse model, calculating thrust curves, variable vehicle mass, aerodynamic drag, and apogee events.

- **Monte Carlo Flight Dispersion**: Executes up to 500 stochastic runs using a deterministic SplitMix32 PRNG and Box-Muller Gaussian sampling to model wind shear, rod tip-off, motor impulse jitter, and landing dispersion footprints.

---

### 2. What benefits does it have?

- **Zero-Install, Cross-Platform Accessibility**: Traditional rocketry software (e.g., OpenRocket, RockSim, RASAero) requires Java runtimes, desktop installations, or paid licenses. !NotRocketScience runs instantly in any modern web browser on laptops, tablets, and smartphones.

- **Immediate Visual & Aerodynamic Feedback**: Real-time CG and CP markers dynamically update as components are resized, teaching users the physics of rocket stability before they ever launch.

- **Safety & Risk Mitigation**: The integrated Monte Carlo simulation models real-world atmospheric turbulence, weathercocking, and parachute deployment delays, helping amateur rocketeers, student teams, and educational clubs predict drift zones and avoid rocket loss or hazard.

- **Modern Blueprint Aesthetics**: Replaces dated 90s-era desktop interfaces with an intuitive, clean aerospace blueprint design, interactive Chart.js telemetry plots, and Leaflet GIS ground-track mapping.

---

### 3. What is the intended impact of the project?

- **Democratizing STEM & Aerospace Education**: Bridges the gap between complex textbook aerodynamics and hands-on experimentation for K-12 students, university rocketry clubs, and citizen scientists.

- **Supporting Model & High-Power Rocketry Teams**: Equips high-power rocketry (NAR/TRA) competitors and university teams (e.g., Spaceport America Cup) with an agile rapid-prototyping tool to evaluate custom motor curves, stability margins, and landing footprints on the fly.

- **Inspiring the Artemis Generation**: By combining cinematic space exploration with real physics formulas, it sparks curiosity and empowers learners to design and simulate their own missions beyond Earth's atmosphere.

---

### 4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

- **Programming Languages**: JavaScript (ES6+ / React JSX), HTML5 Canvas & WebGL, CSS3 / Modern Glassmorphism.

- **Frontend Framework & Tooling**:

- **React 18 & Vite**: High-performance single-page application framework and build pipeline.

- **React Router**: Client-side SPA routing (`/` Mission Launchpad, `/designer` CAD Simulator).

- **3D Graphics & Physics Engines**:

- **Three.js & @react-three/fiber**: Custom 3D mesh renderers, procedural geometries, and lighting pipelines.

- **@react-three/drei**: Camera management, loaders, and controls.

- **Custom RK4 Physics Engine**: Proprietary JavaScript implementation of 4th-Order Runge-Kutta numerical integration and Barrowman equations.

- **Visualization & Animation**:

- **Chart.js**: Multi-axis telemetry graphs (Altitude, Velocity, Acceleration, Mach number, Dynamic Pressure).

- **Leaflet.js**: 2D GIS planetary mapping for landing footprint visualization.

- **Framer Motion & GSAP**: Fluid cinematic UI transitions, HUD telemetry overlays, and scroll physics.

- **Assets & Data**:

- **NASA Blue Marble**: Authentic 8K day, night, and cloud planetary texture maps.

- **Standard Solid Motor Database**: Digitized thrust curves for Estes, AeroTech, and Cesaroni motors.

- **Cloud Infrastructure & Deployment**:

- **Vercel**: Edge network deployment, CDN caching, and automated production CI/CD.

---

### 5. How is your project creative?

- **Seamless Narrative Flow (Space-to-Launchpad)**: Instead of dropping users directly into an intimidating CAD form, the project opens with a cinematic, scroll-interpolated space journey from deep orbit down to Earth’s cloud tops, seamlessly transitioning into the mission workstation.

- **Interactive Multi-Sensory Workstation**: Integrates auditory telemetry cues, interactive 3D longitudinal cross-section cutaways, and live visual vector gimbals for aerodynamic centers.

- **Custom Motor Synthesizer**: Allows creators to draw or synthesize their own motor burn curves and instantly observe the flight envelope changes in real time.

- **Stochastic "Spaghetti" Telemetry Visualizations**: Rather than single-line ideal trajectories, the application visually plots hundreds of perturbed Monte Carlo flight arcs overlaid onto satellite maps, making statistical uncertainty tangible and intuitive.

---

### 6. What factors did your team consider?

1. **Aerodynamic & Mathematical Fidelity**:

- Strictly derived Barrowman equations for thin-walled tubes, conical transitions, and fin interference factors ($K_{fb}$).

- Barometric atmospheric decay based on the International Standard Atmosphere (ISA) to ensure altitude calculations remain valid up through the stratosphere.

2. **Computational Performance (60 FPS Target)**:

- Optimized Three.js draw calls, GPU hardware acceleration (`powerPreference: "high-performance"`), and off-screen canvas rendering.

- Employed SplitMix32 integer-bitwise PRNG and Box-Muller transforms so 500-run Monte Carlo simulations compute in milliseconds without freezing the UI.

3. **Accessibility & Universal Design**:

- Implemented OS-level `prefers-reduced-motion` detection, providing vestibular-safe keyframe defaults for users sensitive to motion.

- Clean, high-contrast light aerospace blueprint theme (`#e9eff7`) with legible typography (Inter and Space Grotesk) to improve readability over traditional dark-only CLI interfaces.

4. **Deployability & Client-Side Reliability**:

- Engineered the simulation engine to be completely self-contained in client-side WebGL and JavaScript, eliminating backend server dependencies or compute costs and ensuring 100% offline uptime once loaded.
